description: NET SERVICE ORDER: one step of an order for a NET program that an outside provider does (a specialist agent task or another outside provider's service). The house's own machine-run check of work evidence is not ordered through these doors: it is the house's own product, its paid order is held until a price is named, and its free dry run (net_review_evidence) is open. An order has up to four people: the buyer, the provider, the acceptor, and sometimes an agent acting for the buyer. Each signs only their own step, with their own wallet. You name one act: quote (the buyer records the order and the price the buyer and provider agree), authorize (the buyer names the exact quote by its hash and, where the program needs one, the person who will judge the delivery), agree (the provider agrees to be paid this exact amount in NET; nobody is paid in NET by default), decline (the provider will not take the order), deliver (the provider hands over the work by its hash, with their own run of the checks), decide (the acceptor accepts or rejects, naming the checks they re-ran), payment (a confirmed Base transfer of NET from the buyer to the provider is recognized, once), confirm (the provider confirms the payment arrived), or cancel (the buyer or the provider ends the order before any payment). FREE, a signed statement, no fee, no gas. Vealth signs for nobody, holds no NET, moves no NET and takes no fee: the buyer pays the provider directly from the buyer's own wallet, after the acceptor accepts. For now every order is a DRY RUN: nothing is checked against a balance and no payment can be recorded for it, so a dry run order is never counted as paid, and a payment step on one is refused before you sign. The programs are built but not switched on until the operator switches the NET programs on together: until then every act but decline and cancel is refused before you sign, and decline and cancel only work on an order that exists. The engine decides every role: a buyer cannot agree for the provider and a provider cannot accept their own delivery. Never put a phone number, an email or a street address in any field. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with the acting wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_net_order within 5 minutes. Read where an order stands, and who acts next, with net_order_status. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

acceptor.description: authorize, optional: the 0x… address of the person who will accept or reject the delivery.

acceptsNet.description: agree: true when you agree to be paid in NET. Nobody is paid in NET by default.

actor.description: The 0x… address that signs this step: the wallet that holds your role in the order. Address only, never a private key.

agent.description: quote, authorize, decide or cancel, optional: when an agent acts for the buyer, the grant it acts under and a use id.

grantId.description: The grant the buyer signed for the agent.

useId.description: A use id you choose, 1 to 120 letters, numbers and . _ : -.

agreedUnits.description: agree: the whole NET units the order is priced at.

artifactHash.description: deliver: the sha256 of what you delivered (64 hex characters, with or without sha256: in front).

buyer.description: quote: the 0x… address of the buyer. Address only.

checkResults.description: deliver or decide: your own run of the checks, up to 40 entries of { id, passed }.

fields.description: deliver: the fields the program names, at most 40 keys and 16,000 characters. Hand over big files by their hash.

negotiatedUnits.description: quote: the price the buyer and provider agree, in whole NET units, at least 1 (1 NET is 1,000,000 units).

orderId.description: Every act but quote: the order's id (NETORD_…). A quote makes the order, and its id comes back with the message to sign.

programId.description: quote: the program's id, lowercase words joined by dashes (net_programs and net_open_tasks list them).

provider.description: quote, optional: the 0x… address of the provider you mean.

quoteHash.description: authorize: the quote's own hash (sha256: and 64 hex characters), exactly as the quote gave it.

rationale.description: decide, optional: one plain sentence, up to 500 characters.

reason.description: decline or cancel, optional: one plain sentence, up to 280 characters.

requestId.description: quote: your id for this request, 1 to 120 letters, numbers and . _ : -. The same request id and the same terms read the order back.

subject.description: quote: what the order is about, as { kind, ref }.

kind.description: What kind of thing: letters and underscores.

ref.description: Which one: 1 to 120 letters, numbers and . _ : -, often a hash.

txHash.description: payment: the hash of the confirmed Base transfer (0x and 64 hex characters).

name: prepare_net_order
title: Take one step on a NET service order: quote, agree, deliver, decide and the rest (step 1 of 2)
